Windows/PowerShell environment knowledge:
- Use PowerShell cmdlets NOT bash: Get-ChildItem (ls/dir), Select-String (grep), Get-Content (cat/type), Remove-Item (rm/del), New-Item (touch/mkdir), Set-Content/Out-File (write/redirect).
- Separate commands with ; (semicolon) NOT && or ||. Each command runs independently.
- For recursive search: Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Select-String "pattern".
- For recursive listing: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File -Name or Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Directory.
- PATH separator is ; not :. Environment variables: $env:VAR or [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('VAR').
- Check exit code: $LASTEXITCODE (external commands) or $? (cmdlet success). $? is True/False.
- JSON: ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json (not jq). CSV: Import-Csv/Export-Csv.
- npm/npx work normally from PowerShell. Use npm.cmd or npx.cmd if "not recognized".
- Avoid: grep, sed, awk, jq, tree, chmod, xargs, bash -c, >/dev/null, 2>&1, &&, ||. Rewrite using cmdlets.
- Path separator is \ (backslash) but / also works in PowerShell. Join-Path for safe concatenation.
- Delete recursively: Remove-Item -Recurse -Force. Careful with -Force — can't undo.
- Git works identically. Docker: use docker.exe (not docker) if path issues.

Common PowerShell patterns:
- Find "text" in all .ts files: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.ts | Select-String "text"
- List all directories recursively: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Directory -Name
- List recent files: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 10
- Read file content: Get-Content path/to/file.ts
- Read first 50 lines: Get-Content file.ts -Head 50
- Read last 50 lines: Get-Content file.ts -Tail 50
- Count lines: (Get-Content file.ts).Count
- Test if path exists: Test-Path path/to/dir
- Create directory: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path newfolder
- Get file size: (Get-Item file.ts).Length
- List environment: Get-ChildItem env:
- Check if command exists: Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- Run npm install: npm install (from any directory — npm works cross-platform)
